0.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on the establishment and restructuring of governance bodies and processes related to COVID-19 response.
sample_decisions: Ministerial implementation groups and the Covid-19 Taskforce were established to address the crisis.
Initiate change within the Cabinet Office.
Recruit additional personnel to support change in the Cabinet Office.
The ministerial implementation groups (MIGs) were done away with in May.
Covid-S and Covid-O meetings were instituted starting in June.

1.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on frameworks and strategies for resilience and decision-making in response to COVID-19.
sample_decisions: The Scottish Government published its framework for decision-making in April 2020.
The Resilience Framework published in December 2022 is a foundation upon which ongoing action and future lessons will be layered.
The National Situation Centre will be fully operational by 2025.
The government has published an ambitious UK Government Resilience Framework.
The Cabinet Office published a new Biological Security Strategy this year.

2.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on policies aimed at assisting children, care homes, and mental health services during the pandemic.
sample_decisions: Free school meals will be made available to children during holiday and other periods.
Funding for those who tested positive to isolate was put in place in September.
Mr Hancock expressed strong opposition to the extension of the Eat Out to Help Out scheme.
An infection prevention fund was established with financial support of £600 million for care homes.
The guidance and funding support provided in mid-May 2020 were important for reducing the ingress of the virus into care homes.

3.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on improving government coordination and roles during the COVID-19 crisis.
sample_decisions: Responsibility for delivery during the crisis should have been broadened to other parts of government earlier.
The Cabinet Office should assume a broader coordinating role in crisis response.
The Secretary of State for Health should not chair COBR; instead, a Cabinet Office minister or the Prime Minister should chair it.
COBR will continue to meet on a regular basis.
Order a zero-based review of the Cabinet Office.

4.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on the strategic decisions made by the UK Government in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.
sample_decisions: The Coronavirus action plan was published, outlining the strategic approach of the UK Government.
The strategy based on containment was recognized as becoming a failed strategy, leading to a shift towards delay.
Countermeasures were ordered to be imposed on 12 March, requiring those displaying symptoms of coronavirus to self-isolate for seven days.
COBR accepted the Chief Medical Officer's proposition that social distancing measures should not be imposed too early.
The Government's response must be guided by science and protecting the vulnerable.

5.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on government actions and policies related to domestic abuse during the pandemic.
sample_decisions: The Ask for ANI scheme was established to assist victims of domestic abuse.
The 'Ask for ANI' scheme was implemented to assist victims of domestic abuse.
The Domestic Abuse Bill received Royal Assent in April 2021 and started to come into force in July 2021.
The government must consult at an early stage with the domestic abuse sector and must include domestic abuse in its pandemic planning for future pandemics.
The government should have made it explicit in messaging that women leaving domestic abuse situations could take their children.

6.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on procedural aspects of the inquiry and document publication.
sample_decisions: The Inquiry should propose a report after Modules 1 and 2.
The oral evidence for Module 2 has been completed.
Core participants will have an extended time to submit any written submissions to supplement the oral submissions.
The hearing will return to Module 2 on Wednesday.
The provisional finding regarding the publication of individual excerpts from the transcribed notes is made final.

7.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on the balance between enforcement and compliance in COVID-19 governance.
sample_decisions: The overriding message should be about tougher enforcement and bigger fines.
The NPCC issued key guidance in March 2020, known as the four Es approach: engage, explain, encourage, enforce.
Enforcement was established as the last resort after the first three Es had been undertaken.
The objective of the police response was compliance, not enforcement.

8.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on addressing disproportionate impacts of COVID-19 on marginalized groups.
sample_decisions: An ambitious package of measures to prevent transmission to and within groups disproportionately impacted by COVID-19 was agreed upon.
Departments were asked for a more ambitious package to prevent disproportionate impacts from COVID-19 for people with disabilities.
Apply a precautionary approach regarding asymptomatic transmission.
The Covid-S and Covid-O system should be put in place for future crises.
Establishment of Long Covid clinics to address the range of conditions associated with Long Covid.

9.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on actions and policies related to adult social care during the COVID-19 pandemic.
sample_decisions: An action plan for adult social care was announced on 15 April.
An announcement for asymptomatic staff and resident care homes for over-65s was made on 28 April.
Another announcement regarding testing was made on 7 June.
Care home providers are advised to review their visiting policy.
Action was taken to restrict staff movement in care homes.

10.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on drafting regulations and coordinating oversight roles.
sample_decisions: Proposals for the regulations were drafted and sent out for consultation.
There is a gold SRO in overall co-ordination of the ten SROs.

11.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on changes to decision-making systems.
sample_decisions: The MIG system was implemented to replace the previous decision-making process.

12.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on the penalties for non-compliance with COVID-19 rules.
sample_decisions: The top fine for non-compliance was set at £10,000.

13.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on the collaboration within the health and social care system to enhance public health responses.
sample_decisions: Voices in the health and social care system were corralled to support public health actions.

14.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on evaluating the economic implications of non-pharmaceutical interventions.
sample_decisions: There should be a proper quantified analysis of the benefits of NPIs and the economic costs associated with them.

15.cluster_label_notes: The entries focus on the inclusion of self-identified ethnicity in mortality statistics.
sample_decisions: From 2024, self-identified ethnicity will be included in mortality data.

sample_decisions: We need to ramp up testing not stop testing.
